intended_object: The real-linear map ℂ → ℂ, x + iy ↦ ax + i·by, i.e. the diagonal matrix diag(a, b) in the basis (1, i). It sends the unit circle onto the ellipse with semi-axes a and b. This is read off the docstring and from how the file uses it: its determinant is ab, and it is the linear part of the affine map taking the circle to the ellipse.
explanation: The definition uses `Basis.constr` on the real basis {1, i} of ℂ and sends 1 to a and i to b·i. That is exactly the diagonal map x + iy ↦ ax + iby. The lemmas that follow in the file check that it gives these values on 1 and i and has determinant ab. Degenerate axes (a = 0 or b = 0) are allowed and give the expected singular map. The object is a specific map that belongs to the ellipse example, so being specific does not make it too narrow, and Mathlib has no named counterpart for it. The definition matches its docstring.
